title: Zechariah and Elizabeth
note:
Built from the four curriculum photographs in Drive’s “01 - Curriculum Source” for Beginner / Chapter 13 — the opener (p.59), the lesson with the first two questions (p.60), the rest of the questions with “CAN YOU SAY?” and the colouring page (p.61), and the close (p.62). All four are around 2 MB and were read by eye at full size.

The chapter’s “06 - Memory Verse” folder is empty, which is right for this class: Beginner prints its memory verse on the chapter’s own closing page, and Psalm 127:3 was read from p.62.

**No artwork yet.** “04 - Story Artwork” is empty, so the story is twenty-one text cards and nothing carries a picture. Every panel name is here so the drawings drop in without a content change — and when they do, the text cards come out, as they did for Chapters 5 to 12.

**Twelve questions and four games.** Four is this band’s ceiling and twelve is the longest list this class has had, so the games carry two or three interactions each and name every question they answer. The grouping follows the lesson’s own joints: the family and its one sorrow, the angel and everything he said, the months Zechariah could not speak, and who was who.

Questions 11 and 12 come from “CAN YOU SAY?” rather than “TELL THE ANSWERS”. Question 11 asks a child what their own family should be like and has no printed answer, so its game shows the lesson’s list and marks nothing.

The chapter has two prayers and both are printed in full, unlike Chapter 12 where both were stage directions. The opener on p.59 is “Dear God who hears our prayers, teach us to pray properly. Amen” — the book prints no full stop after that Amen — and the close on p.62 is the one carried in `prayer` below.

story.text: Zechariah was a priest in the Jerusalem temple. His wife was Elizabeth.
Both were elderly. Theirs was a family that lived with God.
They prayed to God every day. They only did good to others.
They did not fail to obey God’s commandments.
No one had anything bad to say about them.
But they had a problem. They had no children.
They cried and prayed to God for a baby.
One day Zechariah was offering incense in the temple.
People were praying outside.
Suddenly God’s angel Gabriel appeared before Zechariah.
“Don’t be afraid, Zechariah! God has heard your prayer.”
“Your wife Elizabeth will give birth to a son. Name him John.”
Zechariah was surprised. He wondered how this could happen.
“You did not believe my words. You will not speak until it happens.”
After the service Zechariah came out. He could not speak.
People were surprised. Zechariah used signs to tell them.
After a few months, Elizabeth gave birth to a baby.
As the angel had said, they named the child John.
At that moment Zechariah opened his mouth and spoke again.
That baby grew up to be John the Baptist. He baptized Jesus.
People call him the one who came before Jesus.

curriculum.source: Beginners Mar Thoma Vol-1, Chapter 13 “ZECHARIAH AND ELIZABETH”, pp.60–61 — “TELL THE ANSWERS” and “CAN YOU SAY?”
curriculum.note:
Transcribed from the curriculum photographs, read at full size. Both printed exercises go into this one list, numbered straight through — questions 1 to 10 from “TELL THE ANSWERS”, questions 11 and 12 from “CAN YOU SAY?” — so that the one rule, every question covered by a game, covers both. Chapter 10 set that precedent.

Twelve is the longest list this class has had; Chapter 11 had nine and Chapter 12 had eight. Every answer below is quoted from the printed lesson on p.60. There is no answer key in these pages and there are no teacher’s pen marks anywhere in this chapter.

p.61 also sets “Colour the picture” — the angel appearing to Zechariah at the altar of incense — which is a pencil activity and has no game here.

questions.question: What are the features of Zechariah’s family?
questions.objective: Know that theirs was a family that lived with God.
questions.answer: They lived with God. “Theirs was a family that lived with God. They used to pray to God every day. They only did good to others. They did not fail to obey God’s commandments. No one had anything bad to say about them.” (p.60)

questions.question: What was Zechariah and Elizabeth’s problem?
questions.objective: Know that they had no children.
questions.answer: They had no children. “But they had a problem. They had no children.” (p.60)

questions.question: What did they do about their problem?
questions.objective: Know that they cried and prayed to God regularly for a baby.
questions.answer: They prayed. “They cried and prayed to God regularly for a baby.” (p.60)

questions.question: What was the name of the angel who appeared to Zechariah?
questions.objective: Know that the angel was Gabriel.
questions.answer: Gabriel. “Suddenly the God’s angel Gabriel appeared before Zechariah.” (p.60)

questions.question: What did the angel of God say to Zechariah?
questions.objective: Know the angel’s words — do not be afraid, God has heard, Elizabeth will have a son, name him John.
questions.answer: “Don’t be afraid, Zechariah! God has heard your prayer. Your wife Elizabeth will give birth to a son. Name him John.” (p.60)

questions.question: What are the names of John the Baptist’s parents?
questions.objective: Know that they were Zechariah and Elizabeth.
questions.answer: Zechariah and Elizabeth. “Zechariah was a priest in the Jerusalem temple. His wife’s name was Elizabeth.” … “That baby grew up to be John the Baptist.” (p.60)

questions.question: Who baptized Jesus?
questions.objective: Know that John the Baptist baptized Jesus.
questions.answer: John the Baptist. “That baby grew up to be John the Baptist, who baptized Jesus.” (p.60)

questions.question: What did the angel say regarding naming the baby?
questions.objective: Know that the angel said to name him John.
questions.answer: “Name him John.” (p.60) And it happened: “As the angel had said, they named the child John.”

questions.question: What happened to Zechariah when he doubted angel’s words?
questions.objective: Know that he was unable to speak until it happened.
questions.answer: He lost his speech. “Because you do not believe this word of mine, you will not be able to speak until it happens.” … “when Zechariah came out, he was unable to speak.” (p.60)

questions.question: When did Zechariah get back his ability to speak?
questions.objective: Know that he spoke again at the moment they named the child John.
questions.answer: When the baby was named. “As the angel had said, they named the child John. At that moment, Zechariah opened his mouth and spoke again.” (p.60)

questions.question: What are the features that our family should have?
questions.objective: Meet what the lesson says a family that lives with God looks like — the same features as Zechariah’s.
questions.answer: **This question is put to the class and has no printed answer.** What the chapter offers is the list it gives for Zechariah’s family on p.60, which is why the game shows that list rather than marking anything.

questions.question: Who gives children to the parents?
questions.objective: Know that children come from God.
questions.answer: God. The lesson has God hearing their prayer and giving them a son, and the chapter’s own memory verse on p.62 says it outright: “Sons are a heritage from the Lord, children a reward from him.” (Psalm 127:3)

games.title: The Family That Prayed
games.objective: Know what Zechariah's family was like, what their one sorrow was, and what they did about it.

interactions.prompt: Turn over what their family was like.

interactions.hint: Everything else about them was good.

interactions.prompt: What did they do about it?
interactions.hint: The same thing they did every day.

games.note:
Questions 1, 2 and 3, and question 11 with them.

The `reveal` is question 1 — five things the lesson says about that family, all true, nothing to get wrong. It is also the whole of question 11, “What are the features that our family should have?”, which the book puts to the class rather than answers: the answer it offers is this same list, so the list is shown rather than marked.

The two choosing rounds are the turn in the chapter: everything about them was good, and still they had one sorrow, and what they did about it was the thing they already did every day.

games.title: The Angel in the Temple
games.objective: Know that the angel was Gabriel, and everything he told Zechariah, down to the baby's name.

interactions.hint: He came while Zechariah burned incense.

interactions.prompt: Turn over what the angel said.

games.note:
Questions 4, 5 and 8. The angel’s name is one fact and a choosing round; what he said is four things at once, so it is a `reveal` where every item is right.

Question 8 — what the angel said about naming the baby — is the last item on that list rather than a game of its own. Pulling “Name him John” out into its own question would have asked a six-year-old to hold the same sentence twice.

games.title: The Quiet Months
games.objective: Follow what happened to Zechariah's voice: he doubted, he could not speak, and he spoke again the moment the baby was named.

interactions.prompt: Put Zechariah’s quiet months in order.
interactions.hint: He spoke again at the very end.

games.note: Questions 9 and 10 in one sequence, because they are one thing with a beginning and an end: the silence starts when he doubts and it stops at the exact moment the baby is named. Asked separately a child can know both answers and still miss that they are the same event.

games.title: Who Was Who
games.objective: Know John the Baptist's parents, who baptized Jesus, and who gives children to parents.

interactions.prompt: Match each one to who they are.
interactions.hint: Two of them are John’s own parents.

games.note:
Questions 6, 7 and 12. Three small who-questions, which is what a `match` is for.

The fourth pair is question 12, “Who gives children to the parents?” — the one the book asks under “CAN YOU SAY?”. Its answer is the chapter’s own memory verse: children are a reward from the Lord. It sits beside the three human answers on purpose.

verse.text: Sons are a heritage from the Lord, children a reward from him.

practice.hint: It begins with who the children are.
practice.note: Stage 1, recognition. The wrong options are ordinary phrases rather than invented scripture — a drill that teaches a child to reject a plausible-sounding verse has put two plausible-sounding verses in front of them, and only one of them is real.

practice.hint: It says the same thing twice over.
practice.note: Stage 2, phrase ordering. Three chunks, broken where the sense breathes. The build checks that they spell the verse exactly.

practice.prompt: Sons are a ______ from the Lord,
practice.note: Stage 3, the missing word. Generated by the Memory Verse agent’s Beginner ladder and used exactly as it came out — prompt, hint and all three options unedited.

Stage 4, full reconstruction — five pieces where stage 2 had three, which is the whole of the difference between the two stages. Phrase chunks rather than single words, as every chapter in this class ships. The build checks that these five spell the verse exactly.

practice.prompt: Where does our verse come from?
practice.hint: The bigger of the two Psalms.
practice.note: Stage 5, the reference — recognised, not typed. `write-reference` asks for a keyboard, and a six-year-old spelling “Psalm 127:3” is a typing test wearing a memory verse. Both distractors are real references this child has met: Psalm 6 was Chapter 11’s verse and St. Luke 1 is this chapter’s own Bible portion, so telling them apart is the thing being learned rather than a trick.

verse.note:
Read from p.62 through the Memory Verse agent: `--fetch --source-dir` over the four curriculum photographs, the supervised read, then `--from-extraction`.

Five stages in the shape Chapters 1 to 9 and 11 to 12 of this class use — recognise, order, fill, rebuild, place. Stage 3 is the agent’s own Beginner rung, unedited; the other four are built by hand on top of it. Chapter 10 shipped with the single agent rung alone and is the odd one out.

The verse is the answer to the chapter’s last question. “Who gives children to the parents?” is asked on p.61 and answered on p.62, a page apart, and the fourth game puts them back together.

Translation is unresolved: p.62 does not name one, which is where every other chapter in this class stands.

No second opinion — the teacher’s editorial Sheet was not available for this run.

prayer.text: O God, help our families to continue in obedience to Your commandments. Amen.
prayer.note: The Concluding Prayer from p.62, word for word.

celebration.message: God heard their prayer, and John was born.
celebration.note: The turn of the chapter, from p.60. They had prayed for years, and the angel’s first word about it was that the prayer had been heard.
